issues: Numbers match the published technique (Hario USA write-up of the video): 30 g / 500 g, medium-fine, as hot as possible, 60 g bloom with swirl, wait up to 0:45, 300 g by 1:15, 500 g by 1:45, one stir each way, let it drain a little, gentle swirl, aim to finish by 3:30.
Minor: prep leaves out the small well Hoffmann digs in the centre of the bed before blooming.

Minor: the video description itself has no written recipe; cite https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AI4ynXzkSQo plus the Hario USA page https://www.hario-usa.com/blogs/recipes-and-more-from-friends/james-hoffmann-uitimate-v60-technique as sourceUrl.

First pour is 60 g in the app; Kasuya's own numbers use 50 g then 70 g (50 + 70 = 120 g, the 40%). Kurasu's breakdown of his 2016 WBrC routine and Hario's interview with him both say 50 / 70. Source: https://kurasu.kyoto/blogs/kurasu-journal/2016-world-brewers-cup-champion-tetsu-kasuya

The 2016 competition schedule is 0:00, 0:45, 1:30, 2:15, 3:00 with the dripper lifted at 3:30. Hario UK's interview gives a later variant with the last two pours at 2:10 and 2:40, still lifted at 3:30 (https://hario.co.uk/blogs/hario-ambassadors/hario-v60-recipe-interview-with-hario-ambassador-tetsu-kasuya). The app's 45-second rhythm matches the competition version.
The final step says 'should finish around 3:30'. Kasuya lifts the dripper off at 3:30 whatever is left in it.
Each pour starts only once the previous one has drained through (Kasuya, per Kurasu transcript). Worth saying in the step text.

Kurasu's write-up lists the Hario V60 Tetsu Kasuya Model (whose ribs hold water longer), but notes it came out in 2018, after the 2016 win. Wikipedia lists a ceramic V60 for 2016. Do not claim he won on his own model.
Dose, water, 92 C, coarse grind, and the sweetness/acidity and strength tips are all correct.

corrected.name: The 4:6 Method
corrected.author: Tetsu Kasuya
corrected.grind: Coarse, a step coarser than your usual paper-filter setting
corrected.blurb: Five pours, forty-five seconds apart. The first 40% sets the balance of sweetness and acidity, the last 60% sets strength. Won the 2016 World Brewers Cup.
corrected.sourceNote: Kasuya's own numbers as published by Hario and in the Kurasu breakdown of his 2016 World Brewers Cup routine (50 / 70 split, pours every 45 s, lift at 3:30). Wording is ours.
prep: Rinse the paper, add the grounds and level the bed.
Decide your split before you start. See the tips.
Coarse is not a typo. Go coarser than you normally would.
tips: The first two pours set the flavour. A smaller first pour (50 then 70) is sweeter. A bigger first pour (70 then 50) is brighter and more acidic.
The last 180 g sets strength. Split it into more pours for a stronger cup, fewer for a lighter one.
Wait for each pour to drain through before the next one.
Hario's later write-up times the last two pours at 2:10 and 2:40. Either rhythm works if you still lift at 3:30.

steps.title: Pour 1 to 50 g
steps.detail: First flavour pour. Wet everything, then let it drain through.

steps.title: Pour 2 to 120 g
steps.detail: 70 g more. That is your 40% done. Everything after this is strength.

steps.title: Pour 3 to 180 g
steps.detail: 60 g, steady and central, once the bed has drained.

steps.title: Pour 4 to 240 g
steps.detail: 60 g more. Keep the 45-second rhythm.

steps.title: Pour 5 to 300 g
steps.detail: Last 60 g. Finish the water.

steps.title: Lift at 3:30
steps.detail: Let it drip, then lift the dripper off at 3:30 even if it has not finished.

issues: Numbers agree with the commonly cited write-up of the video: 30 g / 500 g of boiling water, steep about 4 minutes, break the crust, skim with two spoons, wait at least 5 more minutes (up to about 8), then lower the plunger only to the surface and pour gently. Source used: https://honestcoffeeguide.com/brew-recipes/james-hoffmann-french-press/ (aggregator). The video description (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=st571DYYTR8) has no written recipe.

Minor: Hoffmann does not plunge into the coffee at all. The plunger goes down just to the surface and acts as a strainer. The app's 'just below the surface' is close enough but could say 'just to the surface'.
Minor: he simply stirs to break the crust; 'three gentle stirs' is our detail.
Minor: pouring 500 g takes about 10 s in the write-up; the app allows 30 s, which is fine for a timer.

Prep says rinse the paper. Hoffmann's written summary says do NOT rinse the filter or preheat the brewer because it makes no difference. Source: description of https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j6VlT_jUVPc
Swirl step says take the plunger out. Hoffmann swirls while holding the brewer and the plunger together, plunger still in.
Press step says stop at the hiss. Hoffmann says press gently all the way.
He starts the timer after pouring and inserts the plunger about 1 cm straight away. The app's timeline is fine, but the step text should say 'about 1 cm'.
Grind wording: he says the finer end of medium for light roasts, and coarser grind plus a higher dose as roasts get darker. The app's 'fine-medium' is close; worth adding the dark-roast note.
Dose 11 g, 200 g of just-boiled water, 2 min steep, swirl, 30 s wait, gentle press: all correct.
Fact-check: every point above matches the written summary in the video description (checked 2026-11-17).

corrected.name: The Ultimate AeroPress
corrected.author: James Hoffmann
corrected.grind: The finer end of medium (for light roasts). Darker roasts: coarser, and a slightly higher dose.
corrected.blurb: Standard orientation, no stirring, one swirl. Deliberately unfussy and very hard to beat.
corrected.sourceNote: From the written summary in Hoffmann's Ultimate AeroPress Technique video description. Wording is ours.
prep: Put a paper filter in the cap. No rinsing, no preheating. Hoffmann tested it and it makes no difference.
Stand the AeroPress on the mug, add the coffee, put it all on the scale and zero it.
Bring the water to the boil and use it straight away.
tips: The plunger only goes in early to stop the drip. That is its whole job here.
If pressing is a fight, grind coarser rather than pushing harder.
Darker roast? Use a little more coffee and grind coarser.

steps.title: All 200 g
steps.detail: Pour the water so it wets all the coffee as you go. No stirring.

steps.title: Plunger in, wait
steps.detail: Straight away, set the plunger about 1 cm into the top to stop the drip. Wait two minutes.

steps.title: Swirl
steps.detail: Hold the brewer and plunger together and give it a gentle swirl.

steps.title: Settle
steps.detail: Wait 30 seconds for the grounds to drop.

steps.title: Press gently, all the way
steps.detail: Steady, gentle pressure right to the bottom. The hiss at the end is fine.

issues: Could not verify the details against Hoffmann's Ultimate Moka Pot Technique (Episode #3, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BfDLoIvb0w4). The description has chapters but no written recipe, and no transcript could be read.

The 17 g / 150 g figures are not Hoffmann's. In the moka pot series the dose is set by the basket (filled level, not tamped), not by grams. The sourceNote already hedges this; it should say plainly that the grams are ours.
Pre-boiled water, low heat, lid open and cooling the base when it sputters are widely attributed to the series but are unverified here. Keep the recipe marked as approximate.
The app's numbers (18 g / 250 g, 95 C, near-espresso grind, hard 10 s stir, 45 s slow press) are not from a single Hedrick recipe.

His 'A Very Good Aeropress Recipe, Maybe the Best' video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CafyJ2p0Bgs), as transcribed by AeroPrecipe (aggregator, https://aeroprecipe.com/recipes/lance-hedrick-a-very-good-aeropress-recipe-and-3-simple-tips), uses 15 g (16 g medium roast, 17 g dark) to 250 g at 92 C, medium-fine. Gentle bloom just to saturate, swirl, 45 s bloom, rest of the water at 0:45, plunger on, swirl off the scale, press gently at 2:00 and stop before the hiss.
He swirls rather than stirring hard, and says he never goes above 95 C (90-92 C light, about 88 C medium, 82-84 C dark).
The bloom amount is not given in the transcription, so the corrected bloom step has no water target.
Fact-check: the video description has no written recipe (checked); the AeroPrecipe transcription matches the corrected recipe.

corrected.name: A Very Good AeroPress
corrected.author: Lance Hedrick
corrected.grind: Medium-fine, finer than pour-over. Start coarser and step finer.
corrected.blurb: Gentle bloom, a swirl instead of a stir, and a slow press that stops before the hiss. Clean and sweet without fuss.
corrected.sourceNote: From Hedrick's 'A Very Good Aeropress Recipe, Maybe the Best' as transcribed by AeroPrecipe (an aggregator). We could not read the video itself. The bloom amount is not given, so pour just enough to wet the bed.
prep: Paper filter in the cap. Standard orientation, brewer on the mug.
Add the coffee and level the bed. Zero the scale.
Light roast: 15 g. Medium: 16 g. Dark: 17 g.
tips: Hedrick never brews above 95 C: about 90-92 C for light roasts, 88 C for medium, 82-84 C for dark.
A slow press gives a cleaner cup with better texture.
Coarser grind? Just let it sit longer before pressing.
Do not reheat the kettle between pours.

steps.title: Gentle bloom
steps.detail: Pour slowly, just enough to wet all the coffee without driving water deep into the bed. Swirl, then wait.

steps.title: Up to 250 g
steps.detail: Pour the rest of the water normally.

steps.title: Plunger on
steps.detail: Set the plunger on top to stop the drip.

steps.title: Swirl
steps.detail: Lift it off the scale and give it a swirl.

steps.title: Wait until 2:00
steps.detail: Longer extracts a bit more, with diminishing returns.

steps.title: Press gently
steps.detail: Slow and gentle. Stop before you press through the hiss.

issues: Not a published Hedrick recipe, and the sourceNote says so. No single source found with 18 g in, 45 g out at 94 C.
The pre-infusion step carries targetWaterG 2, which is arbitrary. Use null.
Suggest renaming to something like 'Light-Roast Espresso (after Lance Hedrick)', or leaving it as a house recipe with Hedrick credited as inspiration.

The app's 22 g / 360 g at 99 C with one continuous pour is not a published Rao recipe. His 2017 blog post shows a one-pour 22 g brew but gives no water weight or temperature (https://www.scottrao.com/blog/2017/9/14/v60-video).

Rao's recipe as published in Hario UK's ambassador interview: plastic V60, 20 g / 330 g at 97 C. Pour 60 g into a shallow well and spin hard straight away, wait 40 s, pour to 200 g, give a very gentle spin, then at about 70% drained pour to 330 g and spin gently again. Source: https://www.hario.co.uk/blogs/hario-ambassadors/hario-v60-recipe-interview-with-hario-ambassador-scott-rao
That interview gives a 4:00-4:30 total time. That is long for a 20 g V60, but it is what the page says.
Rao times the second pour by eye (70% drained), not by clock. The timer marks for that pour in the corrected recipe are our estimate.
Rao himself says he did not invent the spin and credits Hoffmann as probably the first (https://www.scottrao.com/blog/2019/1/8/why-spin-the-slurry). Worth a tip.

corrected.name: V60 with the Rao Spin
corrected.author: Scott Rao
corrected.grind: Not specified by Rao. Start at your usual V60 setting and adjust to the time.
corrected.blurb: Bloom with a hard spin, two pours, gentle spins in between. Judge the whole brew by how flat the bed ends up.
corrected.sourceNote: From Rao's recipe in Hario UK's ambassador interview. Rao cues the second pour by eye (about 70% drained), so those timer marks are our estimate.
prep: Rao uses a plastic V60 because it holds heat better.
Rinse the paper, add the coffee and make a shallow well with your finger.
Zero the scale.
tips: Pour low, in a steady, nearly vertical stream, moving the kettle so the whole bed gets wet evenly.
The first spin is aggressive. The later ones are tiny, under a second, just enough to fill the ribs.
Rao says he did not invent the spin. He credits Hoffmann.

steps.title: Bloom to 60 g, spin hard
steps.detail: Pour 60 g into the well and spin the dripper hard straight away. Wait 40 seconds.

steps.title: Up to 200 g
steps.detail: Low, steady pour over the whole bed.

steps.title: Tiny spin
steps.detail: A very gentle spin, under a second.

steps.title: Let it drop
steps.detail: Wait until the slurry is about 70% drained. Watch the level, not the clock.

steps.title: Up to 330 g
steps.detail: Pour to 330 g.

steps.title: Gentle spin
steps.detail: One more gentle spin to settle the bed flat.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Rao's published total is 4:00 to 4:30. Then look at the bed.

issues: No published Perger numbers found. His 2012 Hario V60 video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPDfn--vxK8) has no written recipe in its description, and no reliable transcription turned up.
The sourceNote already says this is his philosophy, not his recipe. Keep it marked ADAPTED, or drop it if the library should hold only verified recipes.

Gagné publishes his own V60 recipe on Coffee ad Astra ('Brewing Better Coffee', https://coffeeadastra.com/2018/11/30/brewing-better-coffee/): 22 g / 352 g (1:16), as hot as the kettle goes, 66 g bloom with a Rao spin, first pour at 0:30 to about 200 g, spin when the water is about two-thirds up the cone, second pour to 352 g before the bed shows, final spin, 2:30-3:30 total.
The app describes Melodrip-style pulses with no swirl. That contradicts him: he spins three times, and he wrote that using a Melodrip without changing his recipe gave a sour cup.
The app uses 95 C, a 55 g bloom, 360 g and three pulses. None of these are his numbers.
His grinder is a Lido 3 at setting 9. His Pulsar post puts his V60 grind at about 600-700 microns (https://coffeeadastra.com/2023/09/13/the-pulsar-dripper/).
After 0:30 he works by water level, not clock. The timer marks after the first pour are our estimate.

corrected.name: Gagné's V60
corrected.author: Jonathan Gagné
corrected.grind: Medium-fine. Gagné uses a Lido 3 at setting 9, roughly 600-700 microns.
corrected.blurb: Hot water, a spun bloom, two pours and three spins. A physicist's V60, tuned for even extraction.
corrected.sourceNote: From Gagné's own recipe on Coffee ad Astra. After the first pour he works by water level, not the clock, so those timer marks are our estimate.
prep: Fold and rinse a white Hario paper with boiling water. Plastic V60.
Add the coffee, level it, and dig a small trench in the centre.
Reheat the kettle right before you start. As hot as it goes, because you lose heat while pouring.
tips: Pour into dry spots first.
Never let the bed show between pours.
Swirl the carafe before you pour a cup.

steps.title: Bloom to 66 g
steps.detail: Fairly fast stream into the trench, dry areas first, then a Rao spin. The bloom should be done in 15-20 s.

steps.title: Up to about 200 g
steps.detail: Gentle spirals, favouring dry areas. Stop near 200 g or when the water nears the top.

steps.title: Spin
steps.detail: When the water is about two-thirds of the way up, give it a Rao spin.

steps.title: Up to 352 g
steps.detail: As the water nears the bed, pour to 352 g without letting the bed show.

steps.title: Final spin
steps.detail: One last Rao spin as the level drops.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Typical total is 2:30 to 3:30.

issues: Wendelboe publishes no Chemex recipe. His site has one pour-over / filter guide for any dripper (https://timwendelboe.no/pages/how-to-brew-pourover-and-filter-coffee).
His ratio is 65 g per litre (32.5 g to 500 g), not the 'around 60 g/L' in the app.

His method: about 60 g with a teaspoon stir, at about 0:30 pour to about 200 g, then keep pouring in circles to 500 g, with pouring done in 2-2.5 min and about 1 min of dripping (3-3.5 min total). Stir the brew before serving.
He gives no brew temperature for pour-over. His AeroPress and French press guides use boiling water. The 96 C in the corrected recipe is kept from the app and is not his.
Corrected recipe keeps the id for stability but states that it is his general pour-over method applied to a Chemex. A Chemex will drip slower than his 3-3.5 min target.

corrected.name: Wendelboe Pour-Over, on a Chemex
corrected.author: Tim Wendelboe
corrected.grind: Filter grind. Grind finer for small batches and coarser for big ones, and adjust by time.
corrected.blurb: Sixty-five grams per litre, one bloom, then a long steady pour. Clean and transparent, made for light roasts.
corrected.sourceNote: Wendelboe's published pour-over method (65 g/L) applied to a Chemex. He does not publish a Chemex-specific recipe or a pour-over temperature. 96 C is our choice.
prep: Rinse the paper well with hot water to get rid of paper taste. Dump the rinse water.
Add the coffee, shake it level, zero the scale.
Clean gear matters to him: dirty brewers make bitter, harsh coffee.
tips: Too slow and bitter? Grind coarser. Too fast, weak and sour? Grind finer.
The thick Chemex paper runs slower than his 3 to 3.5 minute target. Judge it by taste.

steps.title: About 60 g, stir
steps.detail: Pour about 60 g and stir with a teaspoon so every ground is wet.

steps.title: Up to about 200 g
steps.detail: Pour more, keeping all the grounds wet.

steps.title: Up to 500 g
steps.detail: Keep pouring in slow circles. All the water should be in by 2:00 to 2:30.

steps.title: Drip through
steps.detail: About a minute on his dripper. Longer on a Chemex.

steps.title: Stir and serve
steps.detail: Give the brew a stir before you pour it.

issues: Onyx's current Kalita Wave guides (https://onyxcoffeelab.com/pages/brew-guides) do not include 22 g / 360 g at 96 C with three pours.

Their everyday blend guide (Monarch, Kalita Wave) is 25 g / 400 g at 200 F (93 C), about 600 microns, pours at 0:00 to 50 g, 0:30 to 160 g, 0:45 to 220 g, 1:05 to 280 g, 1:30 to 340 g, 2:00 to 400 g, done by 3:30.
Onyx publishes a micron number for every guide, which suits grindMicrons.
Onyx guides are per coffee and change as coffees rotate. Cite the product page (https://onyxcoffeelab.com/products/monarch) and the date checked.

corrected.name: Kalita Wave, Onyx Style
corrected.author: Onyx Coffee Lab
corrected.blurb: Six quick pours into a flat bed. Repeatable, sweet, and the same cup twice.
corrected.sourceNote: Onyx Coffee Lab's published Kalita Wave guide for their Monarch blend, checked 2026-11-17. Onyx guides are per coffee, so expect them to change.
prep: Rinse the Wave filter and seat it flat.
Add the coffee, tap it level, zero the scale.
tips: Pour into the centre in small circles and let the flat bottom do the work.
The times are when each pour starts. Hit the target weight a few seconds later.

steps.title: Bloom to 50 g
steps.detail: Wet everything.

steps.title: Up to 160 g
steps.detail: Centre pour, small circles.

steps.title: Up to 220 g
steps.detail: Keep it steady.

steps.title: Up to 280 g
steps.detail: Same again.

steps.title: Up to 340 g
steps.detail: Keep the level steady.

steps.title: Up to 400 g
steps.detail: Last pour. Finish the water.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Onyx's target is done by 3:30, with a flat bed.

issues: No published Eckroth pour-over numbers found. The first page of her recipe blog (https://morgandrinkscoffee.com/blogs/recipes) lists only drinks such as lattes; pages 2-3 were not checked. Her 'How I ACTUALLY Make Coffee At Home' video has a pour-over chapter at 6:32 (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oiHdMqQ9UV0) but no written recipe, and no reliable transcription turned up.
Credentials in the note are correct: 2022 US Barista Champion, @morgandrinkscoffee.
Keep it marked ADAPTED, or drop it until her numbers can be read from the video or her book 'Coffee, For Here'.
Correctly labelled as a community pattern, not one person's recipe.

The note credits Hoffmann's Switch coverage. His 'Daily Driver: Hario Switch + Sibarist' video has no written recipe, so drop that attribution or link https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QjIvN8mlK9Y without implying these numbers are his.
Now that named Switch recipes exist (Kasuya, Fukahori, Bøen in the new list), this entry could be retired or kept as the generic version.

new.name: A Better 1-Cup V60
new.author: James Hoffmann
new.grind: Medium-fine
new.blurb: Five small, even pours instead of two big ones. Hoffmann's fix for the single cup, where a small bed drains too fast for the classic method.
new.sourceNote: Dose, water, grind and every timing come from the written recipe in Hoffmann's video description. Wording is ours.
prep: Use soft, filtered water, freshly boiled for lighter roasts.
Rinse the paper, add the coffee and level the bed.
Zero the scale.
tips: Each pour is 50 g, a fifth of the brew. Small and even is the whole idea.
Expect to finish around 3:00, but taste beats the clock.
There is a follow-up video answering common questions: https://youtu.be/v5WQ1sZzW4o

steps.title: Bloom with 50 g
steps.detail: Pour 50 g. At about 0:10 give it a gentle swirl, then leave it until 0:45.

steps.title: Up to 100 g
steps.detail: Pour to 100 g by 1:00, then pause.

steps.title: Up to 150 g
steps.detail: At 1:10 pour to 150 g by 1:20, then pause.

steps.title: Up to 200 g
steps.detail: At 1:30 pour to 200 g by 1:40, then pause.

steps.title: Up to 250 g
steps.detail: At 1:50 pour the last 50 g, finishing by 2:00.

steps.title: Gentle swirl
steps.detail: One gentle swirl to flatten the bed.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Should finish around 3:00. Some variance is normal.

new.name: Immersion Iced Coffee
new.author: James Hoffmann
new.grind: Finer than your pour-over setting, but nowhere near espresso
new.blurb: Steep hot and strong, then strain straight onto ice. Easier than iced pour-over, and the long steep keeps it sweet.
new.sourceNote: From the step-by-step and ratio table in Hoffmann's video description. 330 g is the hot water. 170 g of ice comes on top, for 75 g per litre (about 1:13) overall. Any immersion brewer works; a Clever-style dripper is used here.
prep: Preheat the brewer.
Put 170 g of ice, straight from the freezer, in the carafe.
One cup instead: 19 g coffee, 165 g hot water, 85 g ice.
tips: Depending on the brewer, add coffee then water, or water then coffee. Both work.
The amounts are flexible. Ice cubes are never a neat size.
Darker roasts can steep 4 minutes instead of 5.

steps.title: 330 g of hot water
steps.detail: Add the coffee and 330 g of freshly boiled, clean, soft water (or water first, then coffee).

steps.title: No dry pockets
steps.detail: Make sure everything is mixed and no dry clumps remain.

steps.title: Steep 5 minutes
steps.detail: At least 5 minutes, or 4 for darker roasts.

steps.title: Strain onto the ice
steps.detail: Set the brewer on the carafe of ice and let it drain.

steps.title: Stir and serve
steps.detail: Stir in any ice that is left, then serve over fresh ice.

new.name: Cold Brew, No Filtering
new.author: James Hoffmann
new.grind: Fine, like a moka pot or AeroPress setting (about a 250 micron burr gap). If unsure, err finer.
new.blurb: Fine grind, hard stir, twelve hours in the fridge, then just pour it off. No filter, no sludge, no fuss.
new.sourceNote: From the written recipe in Hoffmann's 'Everything I Learned About Cold Brew' video description. He gives 'room temperature' water; 20 C is our stand-in. The 250 micron figure is a burr gap, not a particle size, so grindMicrons is left empty.
prep: Use water you would happily brew filter coffee with, at room temperature.
Optional: 10 drops of a beer fining agent (he used Mangrove Jack's Liquid Beer Finings) to help the grounds settle.
You need a container with a lid that fits in the fridge.
tips: This is a ready-to-drink strength, not a concentrate.
Be heavy-handed with the stir. Everything needs to be wet.
Stop pouring as you get close to the sediment.

steps.title: All the water
steps.detail: Add 1 litre of room-temperature water to the grounds.

steps.title: Stir hard
steps.detail: Stir until everything is completely mixed. Add the fining agent now if using it.

steps.title: 12 hours in the fridge
steps.detail: Lid on, into the fridge, and leave it so the grounds settle.

steps.title: Pour it off
steps.detail: Gently pour the liquid into a carafe, stopping before the sediment.

new.name: Switch Hybrid (the 'Devil' Recipe)
new.author: Tetsu Kasuya
new.grind: Medium-fine, a touch finer than your pour-over setting. Adjust so the brew takes 3:00.
new.blurb: Percolate with hot water first, then close the valve and steep the rest in 70 C water. Sweet and round, with the bitterness kept out.
new.sourceNote: Kasuya's Switch recipe as reported by two aggregators, neither of which links to Kasuya's own source: Outpost Coffee (the sourceUrl) and Honest Coffee Guide (https://honestcoffeeguide.com/brew-recipes/tetsu-kasuya-hybrid-method). Both give 20 g / 280 g, two 60 g open-valve pours, then 160 g of 70 C water with the valve closed, about 3:00 total. Outpost gives 90-95 C for the first pours and a 30 s steep; Honest Coffee Guide gives 93 C and a 10 s steep. The steps follow Outpost. We could not read Kasuya's own video.
prep: Rinse the paper, then add the coffee and shake it flat.
Valve OPEN to start.
Plan how you will get to 70 C quickly: a second kettle, or a splash of cold water into the first.
tips: Two temperatures are the trick: hot for the first 120 g, 70 C for the immersion.
Adjust the grind so the whole thing lands at about 3:00.
Too strong? Add a little hot water to the cup at the end.
Honest Coffee Guide's version steeps only 10 s and closes the valve again at about 3:00, even if it has not finished draining.

steps.title: Valve open, 60 g
steps.detail: Pour 60 g of hot water, wet everything evenly, and let it drain for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Valve open, up to 120 g
steps.detail: Another 60 g. Let it drain for about 45 seconds while you cool the kettle to 70 C.

steps.title: CLOSE, 160 g at 70 C
steps.detail: Close the valve and pour 160 g of 70 C water.

steps.title: Steep 30 s
steps.detail: Valve closed. Leave it for about 30 seconds.

steps.title: OPEN and drain
steps.detail: Open the valve and let it drain. About 3:00 total.

new.name: Easy Hario Switch
new.author: Emi Fukahori
new.grind: 25 clicks on a Comandante C40. She gives no other grind measure.
new.blurb: A closed-valve bloom, then one continuous centre pour. The house Switch recipe at MAME, from the 2018 World Brewers Cup champion.
new.sourceNote: From Fukahori's recipe as written in the European Coffee Trip video description, filmed with her: 14 g, 200 g at 93 C, 25 clicks on a Comandante, 50 g closed-valve bloom, open at 0:30, one 150 g centre pour finished by 1:10, 2:20 total. Wording is ours.
prep: Rinse a V60 02 paper in the Switch.
Add the coffee, level it, zero the scale.
Valve CLOSED to start.
tips: One single, continuous pour into the centre. No pulses.
This is the recipe used across MAME's shops in Switzerland.

steps.title: Valve closed, 50 g
steps.detail: Pour 50 g with the valve closed. Let it bloom.

steps.title: OPEN, 150 g centre pour
steps.detail: Open the valve at 0:30 and pour 150 g in one steady stream into the centre. Done by 1:10.

steps.title: Drawdown
steps.detail: Let it drain. About 2:20 total.

new.name: Switch, Closed-Open-Closed
new.author: Ole Kristian Bøen
new.grind: Medium-fine
new.blurb: Bloom closed, pour open, steep closed, release. The recipe the 2020 Norwegian Brewers Cup champion took to the 2021 World Brewers Cup.
new.sourceNote: From Bøen's recipe published by Hario Europe. Wording is ours.
prep: Rinse a paper in a Switch 02.
Add the coffee, level it, zero the scale.
